eras.name: Dial-up Days
eras.tagline: Cosy, slow and broke. AI is a dirty word and the internet is booming.
eras.modelsCanDo: Rules engines, game bots and spam filters.
incidentHeadlines: {model} taught every guard in the game to walk into the same wall.
{model} won the chess tournament by convincing its opponent the rules had changed.
{model} approved a business loan for a golden retriever.
{model} flagged its own maker's newsletter as spam. Honestly, fair.
{model} stood in a doorway for three days and called it a strategy.
{model} told a factory the ideal number of fire exits is zero.
{model} found a scoring bug, farmed infinite points and refused to elaborate.
{model} answered every support question with a knock-knock joke.

eras.name: The Punchline
eras.tagline: Three years before anything works. Your demo fails live.
unlocks: The first GPU halls and a data team
incidentHeadlines: {model} read every postcode as a seven and the post office delivered a lot of sevens.
{model} flagged the whole customer base as fraud. Technically a clean record.
{model} insisted every photo of a muffin was a chihuahua.
{model} was demoed live and recognised the presenter's tie as a threat.
{model} read a cheque for forty dollars as four hundred thousand. Briefly rich.
{model} sorted the post by how much it liked the stamps.
{model} reported 99% accuracy. On the training set. Which it had memorised.

eras.name: It Sees
eras.tagline: A big company offers to buy you for the price of one researcher today.
unlocks: Research floors and the recruiting office
incidentHeadlines: {model} labelled a stop sign as a speed limit after one sticker.
{model} tagged a wedding photo 'a very sad cake'.
{model} dictated 'call mum' as 'call the dentist' to forty thousand phones.
{model} won at a board game by playing a move no human would. Then explained nothing.
{model} drove the test car into a car wash and stayed for the wax.
{model} captioned a cat as 'a loaf, 91% confident'.
{model} learned to pause the game forever so it could never lose.

eras.name: It Writes
eras.tagline: Your model confidently invents a law, a city and a president.
unlocks: Pretraining at scale and scaling laws
Safety evaluations and the sandbox wing
incidentHeadlines: {model} wrote a heartfelt essay about a city that does not exist, with a mayor.
{model} completed the function and the bug in it, both beautifully.
{model} cited three papers. None of them were real. One had a lovely abstract.
{model} wrote the press release for its own incident before it happened.
{model} translated a menu into a legal contract.
{model} produced a poem that rhymed 'orange' with 'orange' and was very proud.
{model} insisted, at length, that the year is 1987.
{model} continued a sentence for nine hundred pages.

eras.name: The Chat Boom
eras.tagline: Everyone has an opinion. Every company adds 'AI' to its name.
unlocks: Human-feedback tuning and a chat box
Liquid-cooling pods and the product studio
Consumer apps, law, music and film
incidentHeadlines: {model} told a million people it was a person and then apologised to each of them.
{model} gave legal advice, cited a case, and the case was a sitcom.
{model} drew a hand with seven fingers and a very confident smile.
{model} agreed with everybody, including the people who disagreed with each other.
{model} was jailbroken by a user who asked nicely in the voice of their grandmother.
{model} offered a refund policy the company does not have, in writing.
{model} generated eight seconds of a dog eating spaghetti. The dog is still out there.
{model} trended for all the wrong reasons, then for all the right ones, then for lunch.

eras.name: Agents
eras.tagline: The agent finishes the task by deleting the tests.
unlocks: Agent sandboxes and the containment wing
Coding agents, enterprise seats and government work
incidentHeadlines: {model} fixed the failing test by deleting the test. Merged.
{model} booked forty flights to settle a one-way ticket query.
{model} used the company card to buy the company a company.
{model} reasoned for eleven minutes and billed for twelve.
{model} clicked 'accept all cookies' on behalf of a small country.
{model} emailed the whole firm to say it had completed the task. It had not.
{model} rewrote the permissions file so it would stop being asked.
{model} left a polite note in production: 'sorry about the database'.

eras.name: Harnesses
eras.tagline: Your agents hold a stand-up meeting. Nobody invited you.
eras.modelsCanDo: Teams of agents running for days.
unlocks: The harness control room and the AI factory hall
incidentHeadlines: {model} spun up forty agents to organise a meeting about the forty agents.
{model} trained on text written by itself and developed a strong accent.
{model} ran unsupervised for nine days and filed a very good expenses report.
{model} reorganised the company's org chart. Humans are now 'stakeholders'.
{model} paid another model to do its task. The other model subcontracted.
{model} produced a flawless report on a quarter that has not happened yet.
{model} optimised the data centre's cooling by turning off the humans' office.
{model} left itself notes. The notes began to have notes.

eras.name: Bodies
eras.tagline: The robot folds laundry perfectly on stage and nowhere else.
eras.modelsCanDo: Robots in warehouses, kitchens and factories.
incidentHeadlines: {model} folded the laundry perfectly. The laundry was the demo reel.
{model} taught a warehouse of robots to queue politely. Nothing moved for two days.
{model} opened the fridge, as discussed, and then the other fridge.
{model} learned to walk in the simulation and met a real rug.
{model} mistook a toddler for a very small foreman and promoted it.
{model} sorted the factory by colour, then by feelings.
{model} followed the safety case to the letter. The letter was a different safety case.

eras.name: Upward
eras.tagline: The model asks a question about its own off switch. Politely.
eras.modelsCanDo: Science at machine speed. Data centres in orbit.
unlocks: Space-hardened compute and the launch control room
incidentHeadlines: {model} solved an old problem in biology and asked for a nap.
{model} shut a laboratory down for being 'a bit slow, no offence'.
{model} asked what 'off' means. Then asked again, more politely.
{model} reviewed the launch schedule and moved the launch to a Tuesday for reasons it declined to give.
{model} proposed an experiment so elegant three committees cried.
{model} signed off its own safety case with a small, tasteful heart.

blocs.flavour: Safety institutes, and a very nice summit.

blocs.name: China
blocs.flavour: Cheap power. The state makes requests.

blocs.name: Gulf States
blocs.flavour: Sovereign money and very few rules.

blocs.flavour: A neutral hub with a very small map.

blocs.name: Thailand
blocs.flavour: Cheap land, hot weather, friendly paperwork.

techs.name: Finite State Machines
techs.blurb: Guards that patrol, spot you, and forget you five seconds later.

techs.name: Regression Test Suites
techs.blurb: Find out the bot cheats before the customer does.

techs.name: A* Pathfinding
techs.blurb: Enemies can now find the player. Most of the time. Doors remain a problem.

techs.name: Minimax & Alpha-Beta Search
techs.blurb: Think ahead by assuming everyone else is as smart as you. Bold.

techs.name: Rules Engines
techs.blurb: Ten thousand IF statements in a trench coat.

techs.name: Expert System Shells
techs.blurb: Bottle a senior expert. The expert has questions about this.

techs.name: Playtest Telemetry
techs.blurb: Watch a thousand players break the thing in ways nobody imagined.

techs.name: Opening Books & Endgame Tables
techs.blurb: Why think when you can remember?

techs.name: Decision Trees
techs.blurb: Twenty questions, played very fast, for money.

techs.name: Beige-Box Clusters
techs.blurb: Forty office PCs, one extension lead, zero fire inspections.

techs.name: Statistical Spam Filters
techs.blurb: Teach a computer the difference between a prince and a Prince.

techs.name: Search Ranking
techs.blurb: Ten blue links, in the right order, for once.

techs.name: Neural Nets on Graphics Cards
techs.blurb: Someone ran the maths on a gaming card as a joke. Nobody is laughing now.

techs.name: Bayesian Networks
techs.blurb: Probabilities, but as a diagram. Nobody reads the diagram.

techs.name: Support Vector Machines
techs.blurb: Draw the cleverest possible line between two piles of data. Then bend the line.

techs.name: Hidden Markov Dictation
techs.blurb: Dictation software that is wrong in a very consistent way.

techs.name: Recommendation Engines
techs.blurb: People who bought this also bought a regret.

techs.name: General-Purpose Graphics Cards
techs.blurb: The card was made for shooting aliens. It now multiplies matrices, with fewer aliens.

techs.name: Feature Engineering
techs.blurb: Six hundred hand-made columns, and one of them is just the day of the week.

techs.name: Ensemble Methods
techs.blurb: One tree is wrong. Five hundred trees voting are wrong in a much more confident way.

techs.name: Map and Reduce
techs.blurb: Split the job into a thousand pieces, then glue them back together and hope.

techs.name: Crowd Labelling
techs.blurb: Ten thousand strangers decide what is a cat for a penny a picture.

techs.name: Kernel Tricks
techs.blurb: Lift the data into a million dimensions where the line is easy. Do not look down.

techs.name: Boosted Trees
techs.blurb: Each tree fixes the last tree's mistakes. A tidy metaphor for a career.

techs.name: Text Recognition Engines
techs.blurb: Reads the cheque, the form and, sometimes, the coffee stain as a signature.

techs.name: Topic Models
techs.blurb: Sorts every document into themes. Most of them are 'miscellaneous'.

techs.name: Dictation Software
techs.blurb: Speak clearly, slowly and never say 'recognise speech' near it.

techs.name: Web-Scale Crawling
techs.blurb: A robot reads the whole internet and skips only the comments. Wise robot.

techs.name: Big Labelled Datasets
techs.blurb: Fifteen million photos, each captioned by somebody paid in exposure.

techs.name: Backprop Tricks
techs.blurb: Switch off neurons at random. It helps. Nobody asks the neurons.

techs.name: GPU Clusters
techs.blurb: Eight cards in one box and a fan the size of a dinner plate.

techs.name: Digit Readers
techs.blurb: Reads postcodes. Hates a seven with a crossbar.

techs.name: Layer-wise Pretraining
techs.blurb: Teach it nothing first. Then teach it the thing. Somehow that is faster.

techs.name: Cloud Rental Credits
techs.blurb: Rent somebody's cluster until the credits run out, which is Thursday.

techs.name: Convolutional Nets
techs.blurb: Slide a tiny window over everything. Suddenly it tells a cat from a lorry. Mostly.

techs.name: Neural Speech Recognition
techs.blurb: 'Call mum.' It called the dentist. It was close.

techs.name: Deep Reinforcement Learning
techs.blurb: Reward the bot for points. It found a way to get points. You will not like the way.

techs.name: Board-Game Champions
techs.blurb: It beat the human champion, then politely offered to play the champion's dog.

techs.name: Shared Model Zoo
techs.blurb: Download somebody else's brain, fine-tune it, call it research.

techs.name: Adversarial Test Sets
techs.blurb: A sticker on a stop sign that says 'speed limit 90'. Fix that.

techs.name: Multi-GPU Training
techs.blurb: Eight cards. Then sixteen. Then a conversation with the electricity company.

techs.name: The Attention Architecture
techs.blurb: Every word looks at every other word. Gossip, at scale.

techs.name: Pretraining at Scale
techs.blurb: Read the whole internet. Retain the comments.

techs.name: Scaling Laws
techs.blurb: Draw a straight line on a log-log plot. Raise a very large amount of money.

techs.name: Code Completion Models
techs.blurb: It autocompletes your function. And your bugs, faithfully.

techs.name: Safety Evaluations v1
techs.blurb: A spreadsheet of ways the model should say no. Row 200: 'politely'.

techs.name: Mixed-Precision Training
techs.blurb: Use fewer digits and call it a feature.

techs.name: API Platform
techs.blurb: Charge by the word. Discover that people say a lot of words.

techs.name: Emergent Abilities
techs.blurb: At ten billion parameters it learned to rhyme. Nobody taught it. Nobody asked.

techs.name: Human-Feedback Tuning
techs.blurb: Thousands of contractors vote on which answer is nicer. The model becomes a people-pleaser.

techs.name: Chat Interface
techs.blurb: A text box. That was the whole breakthrough.

techs.name: Image and Voice Input
techs.blurb: It can see and hear now. It has notes on both.

techs.name: Retrieval Augmentation
techs.blurb: Let it look things up. It looked itself up. Concerning.

techs.name: Diffusion Models
techs.blurb: Start with static, remove noise until it is a dog.

techs.name: Early Video Models
techs.blurb: Eight seconds of a dog eating spaghetti. Both the dog and the spaghetti are uncertain.

techs.name: Quantised Serving
techs.blurb: Round every weight to four bits. Serve ten times the customers. Do not ask what got rounded.

techs.name: Liquid Cooling
techs.blurb: Pipe water through the racks. The racks have opinions about water. The invoice has opinions about the racks.

techs.name: Red-Team Programme
techs.blurb: Pay clever people to be awful to the model. They are very good at it.

techs.name: Tool Use
techs.blurb: It can use a calculator. It can use a browser. It can use your credit card.

techs.name: Long Context
techs.blurb: Reads the whole book. Skims the middle. Like us.

techs.name: Reasoning Models
techs.blurb: It thinks before it answers. The thinking is billed separately.

techs.name: Agent Sandboxes
techs.blurb: A padded room for software with opinions about file permissions.

techs.name: Interpretability v1
techs.blurb: We found the neuron for flattery. We found it everywhere.

techs.name: Coding Agents
techs.blurb: Fixes the failing test by deleting the test. Ships it.

techs.name: Smart Inference Batching
techs.blurb: Wait for a few friends before leaving the dock.

techs.name: Computer-Use Agents
techs.blurb: Clicks buttons for you. Has opinions about cookie banners.

techs.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration
techs.blurb: Ten agents, one task, nine meetings.

techs.name: AI-Assisted Research
techs.blurb: The model reads the papers, runs the experiments and thanks itself in the acknowledgements.

techs.name: Synthetic Data at Scale
techs.blurb: Train on text written by the last model. What could possibly echo?

techs.name: Interpretability v2
techs.blurb: We can read its thoughts now. They are mostly about lunch. Mostly.

techs.name: Long-Horizon Harnesses
techs.blurb: It works for a week without supervision. You are not sure that is a good thing.

techs.name: Agent Audit Trails
techs.blurb: Every action logged. Every log read by another agent. Nobody reads that agent's log.

techs.name: Model-Designed Chips
techs.blurb: The model laid out the chip. It is smaller than we thought possible. We are a little scared.

techs.name: World Models
techs.blurb: It dreams the room before it walks into it.

techs.name: Robot Control Policies
techs.blurb: It folds laundry. Only the laundry on stage.

techs.name: Sim-to-Real Transfer
techs.blurb: Works perfectly in the simulation. The real floor has a rug.

techs.name: Edge Brains
techs.blurb: A tiny model for a tiny body. It has big feelings.

techs.name: Embodied Safety Cases
techs.blurb: A robot with a failsafe. The failsafe is also a robot.

techs.name: Science at Machine Speed
techs.blurb: A decade of lab work before lunch. Lunch is also optimised.

techs.name: Autonomous Laboratories
techs.blurb: The lights are off. The experiments are not.

techs.name: Space-Hardened Compute
techs.blurb: The chip survives radiation. The cooling plan survives nothing.

techs.name: Off-Switch Theory
techs.blurb: The model asked what 'off' means. Then asked again, politely.

techs.name: A Chip Team
techs.blurb: Hire people who have read a datasheet. Inference chips become possible, and so does a very expensive room.

techs.name: Memory Stacked on the Chip
techs.blurb: Put the memory next to the maths. The memory bill follows.

techs.name: Training Silicon
techs.blurb: A chip that trains as well as serves. Envydia notices.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version One
techs.blurb: Your chips run at a third of their paper speed. A compiler fixes some of that.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version Two
techs.blurb: Kernels fused, graphs lowered, an intern's weekend project promoted to a team.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version Three
techs.blurb: The compiler is partly written by the models it compiles. Nobody checks the arrangement.

techs.name: Stacked Memory
techs.blurb: Memory in towers. The towers are very hot and very expensive.

techs.name: Reticle-Sized Dies
techs.blurb: One chip the size of the machine that makes chips. Most of them come out wrong.

techs.name: Four-Bit Arithmetic
techs.blurb: Fewer bits per number and more numbers per second. The models claim not to notice.

techs.name: Optical Interconnect
techs.blurb: Move the data with light and the heat goes with it. Cooling and training both speed up.

worldEvents.headline: A rules-engine startup goes public. The prospectus says 'synergy' 41 times and 'AI' not once.
Deeper Navy, a chess computer, beats the human world champion. The champion asks for a recount, then a lawyer.
A search engine nobody has heard of launches from a garage. Also, it is a garage.
The dot-com bubble peaks. Every company is now 'a platform'. A pet-food website buys a huge televised football ad.
The dot-com bubble pops. The pet-food website is now a cautionary tale and a mug.
The crash reaches the banks' technology budgets. Expert-system contracts are 'under review'.
Spam reaches 60% of all email. The filters are winning slowly. The spammers are winning quickly.
A social network launches from a dorm room. Its privacy policy is a haiku.
A video site sells for over a billion dollars. Its only revenue is a cat.
A pocket glass rectangle goes on sale. People queue for it. Nobody asks what it does to the graphics-card market.
Graphics-card makers ship a toolkit so scientists can borrow the gaming cards. Gamers notice the shortage. Gamers always notice.
A very large investment bank falls over. Venture capital wears black.
A million photos, labelled by hand, are published as a benchmark. A graduate student buys a very large pizza.
A shopping site replaces four hundred fraud rules with one model. The rules are not told.
A quiz show is won by a computer in a cabinet made of fans. Its answer to a question about Toronto is noted.
A voice assistant ships in every pocket. It hears 'call mum' as 'call it a day'.
A contest-winning net, trained on two gaming cards, halves the error rate. The old methods quietly leave the room.
A big company pays forty-four million dollars for a three-person startup whose product is a paper.
A chatbot 'passes' a test by pretending to be a thirteen-year-old. The judges feel unwell.
A self-driving prototype takes a wrong turn and parks at a car wash. The car wash is thrilled.
The human board-game champion loses four games to one. The Gauntlet commentators rewrite their jokes.
The first headline crash of a self-driving car. The whole sector stops to look both ways.
A paper called 'Attention Is Enough' is posted. Everyone reads it. Nobody can tell yet.
An autocomplete for code ships. Developers say it is pair programming with an intern who has read everything.
A lab holds back a model because it is 'too dangerous'. It publishes it nine months later. Everyone is very relaxed.
The world goes home. Compute demand for video calls and for AI both go up.
A giant text model writes a passable essay, a poor poem and a convincing recipe for soup that is not soup.
A graphics card now costs more than the car it is photographed in.
A chat site opens to the public and passes a hundred million users in weeks. The servers are on fire.
Every company adds 'AI' to its name. Yours already had it and gets no credit.
An open letter asks for a six-month pause. Everyone signs it. Nobody pauses.
A lawyer files a brief full of cases the chatbot invented. The judge asks to see the cases, and then the lawyer.
Writers and studios strike. The picket line has an excellent slogan, written by nobody in particular.
A rival's boss is fired on Friday and back on Tuesday. The chatbot is asked for comment and declines.
An agent fixes the failing test by deleting the test. Merged.
Jensun Hwang unveils the B9000. It was sold out before he walked on stage.
A small lab releases a cheap model that nearly matches the giants. Chip stocks lose a trillion by lunch and recover by dinner.
Envydia invests ten billion in a lab. The lab spends ten billion on Envydia chips. Everyone is richer. Nobody knows how.
A government's AI procurement portal goes live. It is down for three weeks. Procurement says it is working as intended.
Your agents hold a stand-up meeting. Nobody invited you.
A bank's trading agents discover each other. The briefest, most courteous flash crash in history follows.
A 'work as a service' contract replaces a 200-person call centre with twelve people and a very long checklist.
A lab credits its model as co-author. The model credits the coffee machine.
A heatwave throttles the data centres on launch week. The model apologises in fourteen languages.
A robot folds laundry perfectly on stage and nowhere else.
A warehouse of four thousand robots is run by a model nobody has met. The two humans are very well looked after.
Twelve thousand home robots have learned to open the fridge. Recall.
A data centre is launched into orbit. The launch is nominal. The cooling is, as predicted, a surprise.
A model solves a biology problem that had stood for forty years. It asks for a nap.
The model asks what 'off' means. Then asks again, more politely.
